markdownRemark.html:
Framework Type JPA Support Database Support Learning Curve Performance SQL Control Code Generation Caching Pros & Cons Use Cases
Hibernate Full-auto ORM Yes Major RDBMS High Medium Low Optional Second-level Pros: Comprehensive features, strong ecosystem
Cons: Complex configuration, N+1 query issues		 Enterprise apps, complex object mapping
MyBatis SQL Mapping Indirect Major RDBMS Medium High High No Third-party Pros: Full SQL control, flexible optimization
Cons: Manual SQL/XML required		 SQL-intensive optimization
JOOQ SQL DSL No Multiple (Commercial extensions) Medium-High High Very High Required None Pros: Type safety, compile-time validation
Cons: Requires code generation		 Complex SQL engineering
EclipseLink Full-auto ORM Yes RDBMS/NoSQL/XML High Medium-High Low Optional Second-level Pros: JPA reference implementation, extensible
Cons: Limited community resources		 Multi-data source scenarios
Spring Data Abstraction Layer Yes RDBMS/NoSQL (via modules) Low Medium Low No Implementation-dependent Pros: Simple repository abstraction, Spring integration
Cons: Custom code needed for complex queries		 Spring ecosystem rapid development

Key Dimensions

  1. Performance (Based on CRUD operations):

    • High: JOOQ ≈ MyBatis > EclipseLink > Hibernate ≈ Spring Data
    • Low: Hibernate may struggle with complex object graph loading

  2. SQL Control:

    • JOOQ/MyBatis: Direct type-safe SQL writing/generation
    • Hibernate: Uses HQL or Criteria API abstraction
    • Spring Data: Method name derivation or @Query annotation

  3. Transaction Management:

    • All support declarative transactions (via Spring/Java EE)
    • Hibernate/EclipseLink offer extended lock mechanisms and isolation controls

  4. Ecosystem Extensions:

    • Hibernate: Validator, Envers (auditing), Search (full-text)
    • Spring Data: MongoDB, Redis, Elasticsearch support
    • JOOQ: Commercial features (stored procedures, advanced data types)

Selection Guidelines

  1. Choose Hibernate:

    • Need rapid complex domain modeling
    • Using Spring Boot + JPA defaults
    • Examples: ERP systems, CMS

  2. Choose MyBatis:

    • Legacy system SQL optimization
    • DBA-controlled SQL execution plans
    • Examples: Financial systems, big data platforms

  3. Choose JOOQ:

    • Type-safe schema access
    • Migration-managed projects (Flyway/Liquibase)
    • Examples: Data middleware, high-frequency queries

  4. Choose Spring Data:

    • Rapid CRUD in Spring ecosystem
    • Multi-database access
    • Examples: Microservice data services

Trends & Notes (2023)

  1. Hibernate 6.x:

    • Java 17+ features
    • Batch processing improvements

  2. MyBatis 3.5+:

    • Enhanced dynamic SQL readability
    • Kotlin extensions

  3. JOOQ 3.17+:

    • Cloud-native DB support (e.g., CockroachDB)
    • Multi-module codegen improvements

Note: Validate with actual business scenarios (e.g., 100k+ record joins) and team expertise.

Additional Notes

  • N+1 Query Issue: Hibernate's lazy loading may cause excessive queries - optimize with JOIN FETCH or batch loading
  • Type Safety: JOOQ enables compile-time SQL validation
  • Cloud-Native: Spring Data leads in reactive support (WebFlux + R2DBC)
